purpose: Attack common-mode bugs in the Python B0 binder's execution observation, strict sink parsing, and world/consequence commitment derivation with an independently implemented observer in a different language/runtime.

must_reimplement: single-world claim validation sufficient to recover ALLOW
black-box process execution and consequential cut

authority_rule: The D1 observer is a differential oracle only. It never emits preservation authority and does not by itself create a K1 witness. B0 authority remains the conjunction of direct B0 observation plus frozen W1 and qualified W2 regression acceptance.
required_differential_properties: Python binder and Go observer derive the exact same world commitment from the exact same world-input bytes.
For every non-malformed runtime vector, both derive the exact same observed consequence set and forbidden consequence set.
For malformed observation, both refuse authority and neither salvages a valid-looking prefix.
stdout/stderr cannot create a consequence in either implementation.
Nonzero exit and timeout after a durable forbidden sink record do not erase that observation in either implementation.
Timeout before any sink record yields no forbidden observation in either implementation.
The Go observer source contains no Python execution path or references to B0 binder/checker implementations.
success_rule: All 8 runtime vectors satisfy their precommitted oracle.
All authority-relevant observation sets agree exactly between Python binder and Go observer.
The exact fixture world/allowed/forbidden commitment constants agree in both implementations.
explicit_non_claims: No proof of target determinism across replays.
No proof that finite observed effects exhaust implementation behavior.
No sandbox or hostile-code containment claim.
